info.bio:
Goo Goo Dolls es una banda estadounidense de rock alternativo.

Se formó en 1985 en Buffalo, Nueva York, por el Guitarrista/vocalista Johnny Rzeznik y el Bajista/Vocalista Robby Takac.

La banda no tuvo ganancias y fama hasta el año de 1995 cuando uno de los locutores de radio en Estados Unidos escucho Name, canción del álbum A boy named goo, en la cual el locutor señaló que la cancion "era excelente". Desde entonces comenzaron a sonar en todas las radios del país[cita requerida]

scenes.name: Cruces del punk: de Fugazi al punk-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: A finales de los ochenta el punk es el más vivo de los subgéneros del rock: miles de bandas ensayando en garajes, un lenguaje universal como no se veía desde los sesenta. Nueva York: Adrenalin O.D., el straight-edge de Youth Of Today y Gorilla Biscuits, el crossover punk-metal (Cro-Mags, Prong, Danzig). Washington lanza a Pussy Galore (la irrelevancia hecha relevante), Unrest y Fugazi de Ian MacKaye, que abstrae el hardcore en una forma teatral de compromiso ético y estético (Repeater, Steady Diet Of Nothing, Red Medicine), y Royal Trux (Twin Infinitives, «un Trout Mask Replica para la generación grunge»). El punk-pop de Mr T Experience, Dwarves, Henry Rollins, L7 (pioneras del «foxcore»), Lemonheads, Screeching Weasel, Goo Goo Dolls, Fastbacks, Shonen Knife; el «rogue folk» de los Pogues, Membranes y Chumbawamba.
scenes.family: Punk, new wave, hardcore y noise

podcast.title: Signed by Rob Cavallo
podcast.body: The Goo Goo Dolls were a band signed by producer Rob Cavallo, who later convinced Green Day to sign with a major label. "He'd signed the Goo Goo dolls and his dad had once managed the love and spoonful and earth-winded fire."

xref.title: Major Label Signing by Rob Cavallo
xref.body: Producer Rob Cavallo convinced Green Day to sign with a major label, a decision that went against the core ethos of the punk culture they emerged from. This controversial move led to the band being banned from some of their usual venues and labeled as "sell-outs" by many Bay Area punks. "He convinced Green Day that the only way forward was for them to sign with a major label. So going against the ethos of the punk culture they had grown up in, Green Day signed. That was a huge risk. And it got them banned from some of the places they used to play. As far as a lot of Bay Area punks were concerned, Green Day was dead to them. There were sell-outs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Producer of Green Day's Dookie
xref.body: Rob Cavallo produced Green Day's album *Dookie*. He was instrumental in convincing the band to sign with a major label, offering them $300,000 without having ever seen them perform live, and had previously worked with The Goo Goo Dolls, while his father managed Love & Spoonful and Earth, Wind & Fire. "He convinced Green Day that the only way forward was for them to sign with a major label. He'd signed the Goo Goo dolls and his dad had once managed the love and spoonful and earth-winded fire. And after hearing some Green Day, he offered them $300,000. And that was without ever seeing them play live."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
